title: Certificates of Deposit: Maturity Notice, Renewal Tier and What Happens When Grace Ends
content:
All of Piedmont Crescent Bank's Certificates of Deposit reach a maturity date and pass through a grace period, after which each either continues into a new term or ends. This page covers the notice sent ahead of maturity, the events of the maturity date, and the outcome once grace is over.

## Before and on the maturity date

The bank mails a maturity notice a fixed number of calendar days ahead of the maturity date. The maturity date brings the term's closing interest credit, and from that date the certificate stands in its grace period.

## Choosing another tier during grace

On a tier that permits a change of term in grace, the owner may elect during grace to renew into a different tier.

## The day after grace ends

If no action during grace has closed the certificate, then on the day after the grace period ends the certificate follows the maturity instruction on its record:

- **Instruction to renew automatically.** The certificate renews into its tier's renewal tier, unless the owner elected another tier in grace, in which case it renews into that one; the new term is dated from the maturity date. An instruction to renew automatically is honored only on a tier where automatic renewal is available.
- **Instruction to pay out.** The earlier clause under which the entire balance went out as a maturity payout, either into the payout account or as an official check, after which the certificate closed, is **no longer in force**; the treatment of a payout instruction is now set by the current payout basis.

Once the grace period is over, any money taken out of the certificate counts again as an early withdrawal, now from the new term.

## Tier settings

| Tier | Maturity notice mailed (calendar days before maturity) | Change of term allowed in grace | Automatic renewal available | Renews into, absent a change of term |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6-Month Certificate | 20 | Yes | Yes | 6-Month Certificate |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | 20 | Yes | Yes | 12-Month Certificate |
| 12-Month Certificate | 20 | Yes | Yes | 12-Month Certificate |
| 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | 30 | Yes | Yes | 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate |
| 36-Month Certificate | 30 | Yes | Yes | 36-Month Certificate |
| 60-Month Certificate | 30 | Yes | Yes | 60-Month Certificate |

## Questions this rule answers

**Into which tier does an 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate renew if the owner changes nothing?** Into the 12-Month Certificate, per the table.

**A certificate set to renew automatically matures on 10 September (hypothetical) and the owner does nothing in grace. From what date does the new term run?** From 10 September, the maturity date, even though the renewal takes effect only when grace has ended.

**The owner chose the 36-Month Certificate during grace of a 12-Month Certificate with an instruction to renew automatically (hypothetical).** The certificate renews into the 36-Month Certificate rather than its default renewal tier.

superseded_clauses: under a payout instruction the whole balance is paid as kind maturity_payout to the payout account or by official check and the certificate closes
